Article Title: Senior journalist Payal Mehta passes away at age of 46; PM Modi, Amit Shah offer condolences
Article Text:
Condolences poured in from across the political spectrum following the passing away of senior journalist Payal Mehta.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Senior journalist Payal Mehta, who worked with CNN-News18, died in Mumbai in the early hours of Sunday. She was 46.Mehta was visiting Mumbai when she developed uneasiness around 2 am. She was taken to a hospital, but died before treatment could begin.Senior journalist Sheela Bhatt shared the details in a post on X."On a visit to Mumbai, she developed uneasiness. Around 2 am she was taken to the hospital. Before any treatment could be administered, her pulse went silent".Mehta was known for her work covering Parliament, the government and the BJP. Colleagues and senior political leaders remembered her as a dedicated journalist who closely followed national affairs.Prime Minister Narendra Modi , home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh , Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and several Union ministers expressed condolences following her death."Payal Mehta Ji was a hardworking journalist who remained firmly connected to the ground, bringing a deep understanding of national issues to her reporting," Modi said in a post on X.He added that Mehta would also be remembered for her kindness and the warmth she showed towards others."Her sudden and untimely passing is extremely saddening. My condolences to her family, friends and colleagues. May they find strength in this difficult hour. Om Shanti," he said.Shah described Mehta as a thorough professional who was committed to providing detailed information on a range of issues."I extend my deepest condolences to her grieving family and friends and pray to God to give them the strength to bear this profound pain. Om Shanti," he said in a post on X.Singh said he was deeply shocked by her death and recalled her commitment to the Parliament beat."She has left us far too soon. Payal was an extremely hardworking and dedicated journalist who covered the Parliament beat with great commitment and professionalism," he said.He recalled that Mehta would often remain in Parliament from early morning until late at night during sessions, closely following proceedings."My heartfelt condolences to her family and friends in this difficult hour. May they find the strength to bear this irreparable loss. Om Shanti," he said.Railways and Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw also expressed grief over the death of his "journalist and dear friend Payal Mehta"."Her dedication to reporting was exemplary. Om Shanti," he said.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said he was deeply shocked by the news."Had just attended her father's prayer service a few days ago. Payal used to be as regular as me in Parliament during sessions. She was a true professional journalist. Heartfelt prayers for her departed soul. Om Shanti," Rijiju said.
Article Summary: Senior journalist payal mehta died in mumbai in the early hours of sunday. She was known for her work covering parliament, the government and the bjp. Prime minister narendra modi, home minister amit shah, defence minister rajnath singh and several union ministers expressed condolences.

Article Title: 'Party of comedians & jokers': PM Modi's mimicry at Rahul Gandhi's event draws BJP ire

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Sunday slammed Congress after a comedian mocked Prime Minister Narendra Modi while sharing the stage with leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi at his "Chhatron Ki Goonj" event in Indore.In a social media post on X, Union minister Kiren Rijiju said the Congress has become "a party of comedians and jokers.""Congress Party has become a Party of Comedians & Jokers!" Rijiju said."They are out forever.... RIP," he added.Union education minister Pralhad Joshi also targeted Rahul Gandhi and accused him of stooping to an "absolute nadir of moral bankruptcy.""Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party have stooped to an absolute nadir of moral bankruptcy," Joshi said."Weaponising a student interaction to mock and insult the late mother of PM Modi ji reveals a shocking lack of basic human empathy and political culture," he added.BJP leader CR Kesavan also criticised Rahul, alleging that the Congress leader had shared the stage with individuals who mocked an elderly woman by referring to her as a "setting" and accused the Congress leader of laughing at the remarks."Rahul Gandhi shared the stage yesterday with cheap, vulgar trolls who insulted our Naari Shakti by mocking a frail elderly Mataji as a 'setting'," Kesavan said.Kesavan further alleged that the incident reflected an "uncouth culture" and claimed that such conduct was one of the reasons Rahul Gandhi had failed to connect with the youth.This comes after standup comedian Pulkit Mani shared the stage with Rahul and mimicked PM Modi during student-focused programme.During the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme in Indore on Saturday, Rahul launched a sharp attack on the government over paper leaks and a host of student grievances.Rahul said the programme aimed to restore the "hope" that students had lost in the education system."We want the hope that was shattered in your hearts to return with renewed vigour. We want you to start believing in education and the system once again," Rahul said.He said curiosity, love and affection, humility, honesty and fearlessness were qualities that define a student, and argued that students who ask questions are essential to building a strong nation."Students do not hate. They treat one another with affection, kindness and mutual respect," the Congress leader said, adding that a genuine seeker of knowledge "cannot be arrogant" and should remain tolerant of differing viewpoints.Earlier, at a Congress event in August, Rahul took swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign policy, suggesting that the PM’s diplomacy is overly associated with hugging foreign leaders.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi and the congress party have stooped to an absolute nadir of moral bankruptcy. Union minister kiren rijiju said the congress has become "a party of comedians and jokers" rahul launched a sharp attack on the government over paper leaks and a host of student grievances.

Article Title: 'Tell us where to come, schools being fixed before our visit': CJP mocks Rajasthan govt
Article Text:
Ashutosh Ranka said the party would continue its inspections of dilapidated school infrastructure across the state.

What triggered the CJP-government row?

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member Ashutosh Ranka took a dig at the Rajasthan government, saying the Bhajan Lal Sharma dispensation released Rs 4,000 crore for 472 schools on the day the "cockraoches entered Udaipur"."And a double coincidence that 30% of these schools happen to be in Udaipur," he posted on X.Mentioning the Ranka's post, another CJP member Sourav Das quipped: "People of Rajasthan, tell us where you want us to come. Article Title: J&K: Fire damages Mata Vaishno Devi helipad terminal in Reasi
Article Text:
The fire started around 3:15 am. (File Photo)

NEW DELHI: A fire broke out at a helipad terminal in Katra, the base camp for pilgrims visiting the Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine in Jammu and Kashmir 's Reasi district, early Sunday, officials said.The fire started around 3:15 am, apparently due to a short circuit, and was brought under control within 30 minutes through the joint efforts of terminal staff, security personnel and fire and emergency services, officials said, according to news agency PTI.The helipad terminal, an important transit point for pilgrims travelling to the shrine atop the Trikuta hills, was closed at the time of the incident.Some computers at the ticket counter and a coffee shop were destroyed in the fire, officials added.The extent of the damage is being assessed. No casualties have been reported so far.More details are awaited.
Article Summary: A fire broke out at a helipad terminal in katra, the base camp for pilgrims visiting the mata vaishno devi shrine. The fire started around 3:15 am, apparently due to a short circuit, and was brought under control within 30 minutes. No casualties have been reported so far.

Article Title: Morning-after pills may get 4 boxed warnings
Article Text:
The proposed warnings will also caution that frequent use may lead to side effects

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Morning-after pills containing levonorgestrel may soon carry four prominent boxed warnings. Govt has proposed that the pills should be labelled clearly as meant only for emergency use, not as regular contraception, not as abortion pills and not as protection against HIV or other sexually transmitted infections.The proposed warnings will also caution that frequent use may lead to side effects and advise users seeking regular contraception to visit a health facility or a registered medical practitioner.Dr Megha Tiwari, Consultant, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Kailash Hospital & Neuro Institute, said emergency contraceptive pills are an important and safe option when used appropriately, but concerns arise when they start being treated as routine contraception. "We do see women taking it repeatedly after unprotected intercourse, sometimes without understanding that it can disturb the menstrual cycle and cause temporary bleeding irregularities, nausea or anxiety around a delayed period," she said."The bigger issue is misinformation. Some women believe the pill can terminate an existing pregnancy, while others assume it offers protection against HIV or other sexually transmitted infections, which it does not," Tiwari said.She added that the proposed warnings were less about creating fear around emergency contraception and more about ensuring women understood its correct role as a backup method after contraceptive failure, rather than a replacement for regular contraception or condoms.The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed the changes through a draft amendment to Drugs Rules, 1945, covering levonorgestrel tablets of 0.75 mg and 1.5 mg. The warnings would have to appear prominently both on the packaging and the package insert.The proposal also seeks to add levonorgestrel tablets 0.75 mg and 1.5 mg as a specific entry under Schedule K of Drugs Rules, along with conditions relating to their exemption from sale-licence requirements.However, the warnings are not yet mandatory. The notification is a draft, with 30 days invited for objections and suggestions.
Article Summary: The proposed warnings will also caution that frequent use may lead to side effects. The ministry of health and family welfare has proposed the changes through a draft amendment to drugs rules, 1945. The warnings would have to appear prominently both on the packaging and the package insert.

Article Title: Mamata Banerjee's Rejinagar pick withdraws from bypolls contest, then retracts
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee faces setback in Rejinagar as her candidate withdraws.

Candidate changes his mind

Nandigram setback came first

TMC split complicates bypoll battle

Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, changed his decision to quit the contest on Saturday, saying he would remain in the race after Banerjee asked him to continue.Chowdhury, a former TMC MLA, had announced his withdrawal earlier in the day, citing difficulties in protecting party workers and introducing voters to the faction's newly allotted 'footballer' symbol.Hours later, he held another press conference and said he had reversed his decision after speaking to Banerjee and receiving assurances of security from the police.Chowdhury told news agency PTI at his home in Murshidabad earlier on Saturday, "It is becoming difficult for me to motivate grassroots workers who have been facing regular harassment. Also, it is an onerous task to familiarise the electorate with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time. In this given situation, last night I informed Mamata di about my decision (not to contest)... Let's see," he said.Later, he announced that he would contest the October 6 bypoll."I will be contesting the bypoll. I have been assured of security by the police after the supremo (Banerjee) intervened... I had a conversation with our party chief, who directed me not to quit the poll fray.I have met officers of the Beldanga police station and they have also assured me and my cadre of security during campaigning.""I am retracting from my earlier decision. I will see to it that none of our workers faces torture. Even if I have 10 activists, I will win," he added.The confusion in Rejinagar came a day after the Mamata faction suffered a setback in Nandigram, where its candidate Sanchita Pradhan Dey withdrew her nomination shortly before the deadline.Dey had met West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari at the state secretariat Nabanna along with her husband Satyajit before pulling out. She had lost her job in connection with a teacher recruitment scam. The reason for her withdrawal was not immediately clear.With no candidate left, Banerjee announced support for Congress nominee Milan Pradhan, calling the Congress a "sister party" and saying the move was aimed at strengthening the INDIA bloc ahead of the October 6 bypoll.Pradhan was later arrested in connection with criminal cases filed against him during the 2007 anti-land acquisition movement in Nandigram.The developments have unfolded amid a bitter dispute within the Trinamool Congress over its name and traditional 'flowers-and-grass' symbol.The Election Commission has allotted Banerjee's faction the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' and the 'footballer' symbol. The rival faction led by Arup Roy has been given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol.Banerjee's camp accused the BJP government of "acting in an authoritarian manner to crush dissent and win the bypoll by a huge margin".BJP leader and Union minister Sukanta Majumdar rejected the charge, saying such allegations were expected from a "party centred on one person, whose activists had carried out attacks on the then opposition BJP after the 2021 assembly polls".With Chowdhury now back in the contest, the Mamata faction has retained its candidate in Rejinagar, while the Nandigram contest remains shaped by the withdrawal of its original nominee and its subsequent support for the Congress candidate.
Article Summary: Mamata banerjee faces setback in rejinagar as her candidate withdraws. Candidate changes his mind. Nandigram setback came first. Tmc split complicates bypoll battle. Follows a bitter dispute within the trinamool congress.

Article Title: 'Delhi a terrifying daily story for women': Rahul, Priyanka slam Amit Shah over teen's gangrape-murder
Article Text:
Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women.

What happened in Delhi case

NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in Delhi, with both questioning the authorities over women's safety and demanding accountability for the incident.Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, criticised the Delhi Police and questioned the responsibility of Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the force functions. He said the teenager was gang-raped and murdered before her body was dumped in an open field, and questioned how the police remained unaware of the crime for days.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi described the incident as a "horrific act of brutality" in the national capital. He also dismissed the idea that Delhi was providing women with a safe environment, saying the city had instead become a source of fear for women."It's unfortunate that Delhi is no longer the capital today; it has become a terrifying daily story for women," he said.Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. He pointed out that the Delhi Police is under the Union home ministry and asked who should ultimately be held responsible for the safety of women in the capital."Amit Shah ji, Delhi Police is under your control. Ultimately, whose responsibility is women's safety?" he said.He also criticised the functioning of the Delhi Police, asking whether its role had been reduced to intimidating ordinary citizens while criminals continued to operate without fear."Or has the job of Delhi Police been reduced to just intimidating and threatening ordinary citizens? Because the criminals are roaming around fearlessly," Gandhi said.Calling for immediate action, the Congress leader demanded that those responsible for the crime be arrested and punished strictly. He also sought accountability for what he described as criminal negligence."The beasts must be arrested immediately, strict action and punishment must be taken, and accountability for this criminal negligence must be fixed," he said.Rahul Gandhi ended his post by linking women's safety to India's wider progress, saying, "India cannot move forward without women's safety."Priyanka Gandhi also raised concerns over the case, saying the crime against the teenager represented an extreme form of brutality. She noted that another minor girl had allegedly been raped just days earlier and questioned whether authorities were taking sufficient responsibility for women's safety."In Delhi, all limits of cruelty were crossed against a 17-year-old girl, and after that, she was brutally murdered. Just a few days earlier, another minor girl was raped," she said in a post on X.Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women. She argued that while there was discussion about women's development, women continued to face violence without what she described as concrete action against perpetrators."No one in the country is willing to take responsibility for women's safety—only empty talk about women's development is offered," she said.She claimed that hundreds of women face atrocities and violence and alleged that victims can struggle to get action from authorities, including the registration of FIRs."Hundreds of women face atrocities and violence, but they cannot hope for concrete action against the perpetrators—FIRs aren't even filed," she said.Priyanka Gandhi also said the issue went beyond the individual case and reflected a wider failure to ensure women's basic rights. She argued that both society and the government had failed to provide women with adequate safety, freedom and equality."Both society and the government have completely failed in granting women their rights to safety, freedom, and equality," she said.A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field, with the police facing questions over the delay in detecting the crime.The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital, with Rahul Gandhi focusing on the Delhi Police's role and its accountability to the Union home ministry.Priyanka Gandhi also referred to another case involving a minor girl that was reported days before the teenager's rape and murder. She used the two incidents to question the wider response to crimes against women.
Article Summary: Congress leaders rahul gandhi and priyanka gandhi vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in delhi. Both questioned the authorities over women's safety and demanded accountability for the incident. Rahul directly questioned the responsibility of union home minister amit shah over the safety of women in the capital.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Employees hid question papers in shoes, paid Rs 8,000 each
Article Text:
File photo: Thane Police arrest three in connection with TET paper leak case

How the papers allegedly got out

Leak exposed a day before exam

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles, with two employees paid Rs 8,000 each to smuggle out the confidential examination material, according to a chargesheet filed by Thane City police.The chargesheet, filed before a Bhiwandi court on Friday, names 18 accused, including alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta, and lays out how investigators traced the leak from the printing press to those allegedly trying to sell the papers in Maharashtra. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding, police said.According to the chargesheet, the leak was traced to Mahim Patran Pvt Ltd, an Agra-based printing press tasked with producing the confidential TET examination material.Between June 15 and 17, two employees and a former staffer allegedly concealed folded question papers inside their shoe insoles while leaving the premises. Security guards frisked their clothes but allegedly did not check their footwear, allowing the papers to be taken outside, the chargesheet said.The state had prepared four separate sets of question papers for the two TET papers to maintain confidentiality and allow one set to be selected on examination day.Investigators allege that all four sets were nevertheless taken out of the press.The employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers, according to the chargesheet.The racket came to light on June 27, a day before the TET was scheduled to be held. Deputy commissioner of Police Pavan Bansod received information that three men were allegedly trying to sell question papers to a Bhiwandi resident.Police then laid a trap using decoy personnel in Kongaon and detained the suspects, recovering four sets of question papers. Officials of the Maharashtra state council of examination later verified that the seized material matched the actual TET paper.The examination, scheduled for June 28, was subsequently postponed.Police have booked the accused under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy, along with Maharashtra laws dealing with examination malpractice. A special investigation team is probing the case.Investigators have identified Gupta, a former coaching-class teacher, as the alleged mastermind. Police said he had previously been implicated in another examination paper leak in Odisha.The chargesheet cites money trails, technical evidence and the recovery of an original question paper from the Bihar residence of a relative of Gupta as evidence in the alleged supply chain. Police said a supplementary chargesheet would be filed as the investigation continues.
Article Summary: The maharashtra teacher eligibility test paper allegedly walked out of an agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles. Two employees paid rs 8,000 each to smuggle out the confidential examination material, according to a chargesheet filed by thane city police.

Article Title: Over 37 lakh appeals pending after Bengal SIR: EC tells Supreme Court
Article Text:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the Election Commission is handling the appeals process adequately? Yes, they are doing a good job. No, more needs to be done. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.
Article Summary: The election commission told the supreme court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in west bengal electoral rolls remain pending. The poll panel told the apex court that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.

Article Title: Over 5.10 lakh people benefited from govt pilgrimage scheme: Punjab minister
Article Text:
Punjab minister Tarunpreet Singh Sond

Punjab tourism minister Tarunpreet Singh Sond on Thursday said Punjab government's 'Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra' scheme has facilitated pilgrimage for 5,10,807 devotees to various religious destinations in and outside the state.He said the scheme aims to facilitate elderly residents who wish to visit religious places by providing them free travel and other essential facilities.The scheme was launched on November 9, 2025, and in its first phase, around four lakh pilgrims undertook journeys to Sri Amritsar Sahib, Sri Anandpur Sahib and Mata Naina Devi, he said.The scheme was expanded on August 12 to include additional religious destinations such as Shri Khatu Shyam-Salasar Balaji Dham, Haridwar-Rishikesh and Mathura-Vrindavan, he said.Under the expanded scheme, people aged 50 years and above are eligible to undertake the pilgrimage. The Punjab government provides AC sleeper bus travel, accommodation and food free of cost to eligible pilgrims, the minister said.Special arrangements have been made to ensure the safety, security and convenience of pilgrims during the journey. A team of general and medical attendants is deployed on every bus, while dedicated teams are stationed at the destinations to facilitate the pilgrims, according to Sond.Arrangements for pilgrims include air-conditioned accommodation with adequate washroom facilities, along with food and other necessary amenities during the pilgrimage, he added.

Article Title: 'How is it possible?' Kejriwal and family get SIR notice in Delhi, EC responds
Article Text:
Kejriwal, family served notices under Delhi SIR

AAP questions names missing from voter list

EC responds to Kejriwal's SIR notice

NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and four members of his family have been served notices by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Notices have been issued to Kejriwal, his wife Sunita Kejriwal, son Pulkit Kejriwal, and parents Gobind Ram Kejriwal and Gita Devi . Kejriwal is a registered voter in the New Delhi-40 assembly constituency.According to Delhi Election Commission documents, Arvind Kejriwal and five members of his family are among 110 voters from ‘Part-51, KG Marg’ in the New Delhi assembly constituency who have been issued notices.The party questioned the move saying, “Is everything happening in this country just to keep the Supreme Lord happy? @ECISVEEP, how is it possible that the names of three-time Delhi Chief Minister @ArvindKejriwal Ji and his family members are missing from the Delhi voter list?”The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), New Delhi, has said notices were issued to former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and his family members as their submitted Enumeration Forms did not contain sufficient details to establish their linkage with the electoral rolls of the last revision in their respective states.The ERO said, “the submitted Enumeration Forms were not complete in terms of details which would have enabled linkage of themselves with the electoral roll of the last revision of the respective states, which were not present in their submitted Enumeration Forms.”In a press statement, the ERO further said that notices were being issued in accordance with procedures established and communicated by the Election Commission to electors who could not be linked to the electoral roll of the last revision or whose linkage showed logical discrepancies.“ As per procedures established and communicated by ECI, Notices are being issued to the electors who could not be linked with the electoral roll of the last revision and those having logical discrepancies in their linking with the electoral roll of the last revision. Electors have to submit a reply/requisite documents to the ERO concerned on receipt of the Notice. Disposal of Notices will be completed by 29.10.2026,” the statement said.The Election Commission also said a notice was issued to Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta after her name appeared in the list of discrepancies during the ongoing SIR process.Following verification of her details and documents, her electoral entry was validated and will be included in the final electoral roll for AC-14 (Shalimar Bagh), scheduled to be published on November 4, 2026.The notices come amid the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2026 exercise being conducted by the Delhi Election Commission. Nearly 47.6 lakh names were removed from Delhi's draft electoral roll published on August 31, but only a fraction of those affected have so far submitted Form 6 seeking re-inclusion.The window for filing claims and objections against the draft roll will remain open until September 30.The draft electoral roll contains 97.5 lakh electors, compared with 1.45 crore registered voters in Delhi when the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise began in June.Data showed that 62,583 Form 6 applications, including those from first-time voters seeking inclusion, had been submitted by September 15. The number rose to 68,043 by September 16.The 47.6 lakh electors excluded from Delhi's draft electoral roll have been categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others following the house-to-house verification exercise. Around 43.3 lakh were marked as absent or shifted, while about 2.8 lakh were categorised as dead and 1.4 lakh as duplicate entries.According to figures released by the Delhi election office for the claims and objections phase, 91,826 applications were received between August 31 and September 16.These included 22,715 Form 8 applications seeking correction or modification of existing electoral entries, 922 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names on grounds such as death, shifting, duplicate registration or ineligibility, and 146 Form 6A applications from overseas electors, besides Form 6 applications for inclusion in the electoral roll.After the claims and objections phase ends, officials will examine the applications and complete the disposal process by October 29. The final electoral roll under the SIR exercise is scheduled to be published on November 4.
Article Summary: Kejriwal, family served notices under delhi sir exercise. Kejriwal is a registered voter in the new delhi-40 assembly constituency. Nearly 47.6 lakh names were removed from delhi's draft electoral roll published on august 31. Only a fraction of those affected have so far submitted form 6 seeking re-inclusion.

Article Title: As monsoon withdrawal begins, season may end with 10% deficit
Article Text:
Monsoon withdrawal has begun

The deficit in rainfall

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The southwest (summer) monsoon, which has so far reported a nationwide deficit of 15% in cumulative (June 1-Sept 19) rainfall, started withdrawing from west Rajasthan Saturday, as against the normal date of Sept 17, IMD has said.The line of withdrawal Saturday passed through Ramgarh, Mohangarh, Phalodi and Khajuwala. "Conditions are also favourable for further withdrawal from some more parts of Rajasthan and some parts of Punjab and Saurashtra and Kachchh over the next three-four days," said the Met department.The monsoon normally starts withdrawing from Sept 17 and the process ends on Oct 15 - a few days ahead of the onset of the winter monsoon in peninsular India.As many as 14 states, including Bihar, Punjab, Haryana and all five peninsular states, have reported a rain deficit of more than 20% so far. The current situation shows that the monsoon season is likely to end on Sept 30 with an overall deficit of more than 10% in the country as a whole - a level of rain deficiency which is considered a drought - even as the low pressure area and subsequent depression over east central Bay of Bengal may cause good rain in east India and coastal Odisha next week.Although the sowing of kharif (summer-sown) crops has progressed well despite the El Nino-linked rain deficit, it does not mean the crop sector is out of danger as regional variations and the skewed timing of rainfall may impact overall yield and sowing during next crop (rabi) season. El Nino, a climatic phenomenon involving the warming of ocean surface temperatures in central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is invariably associated with a harsh summer and weak monsoon in India.Acreage data Friday shows that though the overall sown area for all kharif crops has declined this year by just a little over 1%, water-intensive paddy - the most important seasonal crop that accounts for the most acreage - reported a decline of nearly 4% compared to the corresponding period last year.
Article Summary: Monsoon withdrawal has begun in west rajasthan. The monsoon normally starts withdrawing from sept 17 and the process ends on oct 15. As many as 14 states, including bihar, punjab, haryana and all five peninsular states, have reported a rain deficit of more than 20%.

Article Title: BJP promise in its coastal bastion: Why DK Shivakumar put Tulu at centre in Mangaluru
Article Text:
DK Shivakumar cabinet meeting in Mangaluru

Eye on BJP's coastal bastion

More than just Tulu

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Friday announced that Tulu, spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, would be recognised as an additional administrative language in the region, fulfilling a long-standing demand."Today, we have decided to make Tulu applicable to Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts and declare it the state’s second additional administrative language," Shivakumar told reporters after a marathon cabinet meeting in Mangaluru.According to a cabinet note shared by the chief minister’s office, Tulu would be Karnataka’s "second additional administrative language" in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi.The 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native Tulu speakers in Karnataka, whose population was recorded at over six crore at the time. Kannada is the state's most-widely spoken and its primary official language.This was also the first time a cabinet meeting was held in Mangaluru and not in Bengaluru.The political significance of Shivakumar taking his cabinet to Mangaluru becomes clearer against the BJP's electoral dominance in the region.Coastal Karnataka, particularly Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, has long been one of the BJP's strongest pockets in the state.In the 2023 Karnataka assembly election, BJP won 11 of the 13 seats across the two districts, taking all five seats in Udupi and six of the eight in Dakshina Kannada. The Congress won only two constituencies.This was despite Congress sweeping to power across Karnataka with 135 seats, against 66 for the BJP.The BJP's hold remained intact in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It won both parliamentary seats covering the region, with Brijesh Chowta defeating Congress's Padmaraj R by over 64,000 votes in Dakshina Kannada. Kota Srinivas Poojary won Udupi-Chikkamagaluru by more than 2.5 lakh votes.The BJP responded to the Tulu announcement by alleging that Shivakumar was "peddling soft Hindutva to make a dent in the BJP’s vote bank.""Shivakumar has never made any secret of his firm belief in Hinduism and frequently visits temples, performs rituals publicly and quotes scriptures. He is now peddling soft Hindutva. This was also evident from his rendition of 'Namaste Sada Vatsale' inside the Karnataka assembly," a BJP leader told PTI, referring to an August 2025 incident in which Shivakumar sang a few lines of the RSS anthem.The RSS is the BJP's ideological mentor.But there is a political twist to the Tulu issue itself. The BJP had previously taken up the demand while in power in Karnataka.In January 2023, the then BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai constituted a committee to examine granting Tulu the status of a second official language in the state, months before the assembly election.Significantly, Shivakumar’s announcements went beyond granting Tulu the status of a second administrative language.The Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru marked the Shivakumar government’s first meeting outside Bengaluru, the state capital. Shivakumar claimed the move was intended to recognise the region’s contribution and address its development needs.The chief minister added that a draft notification would soon be issued to invite public feedback on renaming the Dakshina Kannada district to Mangaluru district.He also announced a host of policies for the coastal Karnataka region, introducing a dedicated tourism policy for the coastal areas to treats tourism projects as infrastructure initiatives while offering investors special incentives and extended loan repayment windows.Additionally, the government approved the Karnataka Marine Biotechnology Policy, 2026-31, which paves the way for upgrading the existing fisheries college into the Fisheries, Marine and Blue Economy University and expanding its student intake from 60 to 200 seats.Beyond these policies, the administration unveiled new urban development planning, fisheries sector incentives, and major financial allocations totaling around Rs 32,611 crore—split evenly between rural development and regional growth for Mangaluru, Udupi, and the coastal region.The announcements further included plans to hold decentralised Cabinet meetings across 10 to 12 locations in the state over the next 15 months and the sanctioning of a new medical college worth approximately Rs 450 crore for the region.
Article Summary: Dk shivakumar cabinet meeting in mangaluru was the first time a cabinet meeting was held outside bengaluru. The 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native tulu speakers in karnataka. The bjp responded to the tulu announcement by alleging that shivak kumar was "peddling soft hindutva" shivakumar claimed the move was intended to recognise the region’s contribution and address its development needs.

Article Title: ‘Arrogance of power’: Congress calls out Scindia over his viral video with MP residents over road
Article Text:
Union minister's fiery response to Guna resident goes viral, Congress reacts

NEW DELHI: A video showing Union minister Jyotiraditya M Scindia in a sharp exchange with a resident over a long-pending road in Guna, Madhya Pradesh, has gone viral on social media, with the Congress sharing the clip and accusing the minister of showing “arrogance of power”.The exchange took place after local residents stopped Scindia’s convoy during his visit and raised concerns over the delayed road work. Residents carrying placards also raised the slogan “Road nahi to vote nahi” (No road, no vote), prompting a tense exchange between the minister and one of the residents.In the video, the resident urges Scindia to ensure the road is completed before the next election and warns that people would otherwise not vote.“This is a request that this road should be laid this time. Otherwise, when you come at the time of voting, we will not vote at all. This entire colony,” the resident says.Scindia objected to the manner in which the demand was made, saying, “Do not ever use this language with me. Understood? I am talking to everyone. You come and make a request. It is my responsibility to get the work done. Okay?”The Congress later shared the video on its official X account, writing, “Look at the arrogance of power.”The party also alleged that Scindia “flew into a rage”. The party added, “The moment the public demanded a road, 'His Majesty' flew into a rage.” It further quoted Scindia’s response and said, “The public will soon put this arrogance in its place.”The video comes amid local complaints over the condition and construction of the road. The confrontation was followed by an announcement on the project.At a public programme later, Scindia announced that Rs 3 crore would be sanctioned for road construction from the MLA’s fund, from the quota of Guna MLA Pannalal Shakya. He also directed the district collector to ensure that work is taken up after the monsoon, according to reports.The episode has since shifted attention from the road demand to the exchange itself, with the viral footage prompting renewed discussion on how elected representatives respond to constituents’ grievances.
Article Summary: Union minister's fiery response to guna resident goes viral, congress reacts. The congress shares the clip and accuses the minister of showing “arrogance of power” the exchange took place after local residents stopped scindia’s convoy during his visit.

NEW DELHI: Union minister and BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri said on Saturday the party would seek an equal seat-sharing agreement with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) if the two parties form an alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly elections .“The earlier 22-seat formula will no longer work. The BJP will not play the role of a junior partner,” he told reporters in Amritsar, referring to the previous arrangement under which the BJP contested 22-23 of Punjab’s 117 assembly seats, while the SAD contested the remaining seats.A meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal in August had sparked speculation that the two former allies could renew their union. The SAD had ended its alliance with the BJP in 2020 in protest against the Centre’s contentious farm laws, which were subsequently repealed.Meanwhile, Puri also asserted that the BJP would leave “no stone unturned” to eradicate the drug menace in Punjab. He said the BJP-led government at the Centre was working on a “war footing” to create employment opportunities for unemployed youth in the state.Taking aim at the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Puri claimed that Punjab had reached a “bad situation” under chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s government, alleging “misrule” in the state.“People are feeling insecure. The police, whose job is to protect the public, are themselves feeling insecure,” the Union minister added.
Article Summary: Bjp leader hardeep singh puri says party will seek equal seat-sharing agreement with the shiromani akali dal (sad) if the two parties form an alliance for the upcoming punjab assembly elections. NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah suffered from food poisoning while on a visit to Karnataka on Saturday and skipped scheduled events in Hubballi and Belagavi, senior BJP leader and Union minister Pralhad Joshi said.Shah was scheduled to inaugurate the new academic building of KLE Jagadguru Gangadhar Mahaswamigalu Moorusavirmath Medical College and the 1,200-bed KLE Hospital and Medical Research Centre in Gabbur, Hubballi. He did not attend the programme, with KLE Society chairman and former Rajya Sabha MP Prabhakar Kore saying Shah had stayed at his hotel on doctors' advice after developing health issues, news agency PTI reported.Joshi later said Shah had suffered food poisoning and was "perfect" now. "Naturally, due to vomiting from food poisoning, he had some weakness," he said.Shah's scheduled visit to Belagavi district was also cancelled. He was due to inaugurate the new headquarters building of Sri Beereshwara Cooperative Credit Society in Examba in Chikkodi taluk."Amit Shah should have come here. He suffered ill health due to food poisoning," Joshi told reporters at the event in Examba.Earlier, Joshi, Karnataka medical education minister Sharan Prakash Patil, former chief minister Basavaraj Bommai, Belagavi MP Jagadish Shettar and Sri Gurusiddha Rajayogindra Swami of Shri Jagadguru Moorusavirmath inaugurated the KLE campuses in Shah's absence.Shah had arrived in Hubballi late on Friday.
